root_cause: Serotonin syndrome from sertraline plus tramadol and dextromethorphan

patient.name: Maya Okafor
patient.background: Nursing student on sertraline for anxiety; sprained ankle playing football yesterday.

findings.result: Overactive reflexes, repeating ankle jerks: inducible clonus
Pupils wide, eyes flicking side to side: ocular clonus
Tox screen: sertraline, tramadol, dextromethorphan all present
Loud, hyperactive gut sounds; diarrhea: hyperperistalsis
No clot in leg veins; Doppler ultrasound normal
Hot, flushed, drenched in sweat: diaphoresis, 39.8°C
Fast regular rhythm, sinus tachycardia, no structural problem
Thyroid hormones normal; no thyroid storm
CK mildly raised from muscle overactivity: creatine kinase
CT head clear; no bleed or meningitis signs

treatments.name: Stop drugs, cyproheptadine, benzodiazepine
treatments.why: Stopping the serotonergic drugs and blocking 5-HT2A receptors with cyproheptadine while benzodiazepines calm the muscles shuts off the serotonin overload.
treatments.attending_line: Look at that, someone actually read the med list. Frame it.

treatments.name: Dantrolene (muscle relaxant)
treatments.why: Dantrolene treats malignant hyperthermia, not serotonin excess, so the serotonin keeps building while the drug strains the liver.
treatments.attending_line: She hasn't had anesthesia. Wrong hyperthermia, Doctor.

treatments.name: Haloperidol (antipsychotic sedative)
treatments.why: Haloperidol blocks dopamine without fixing the serotonin overload, which can worsen rigidity and heat, and it prolongs the QT interval.
treatments.attending_line: Great, you've traded one syndrome for two. Efficient.

treatments.name: Paracetamol and cooling blanket
treatments.why: The fever comes from overactive muscles rather than the brain's thermostat, so antipyretics fail while the cause keeps going.
treatments.attending_line: A Tylenol for a chemical fire. Bold strategy.

post_mortem: Maya was already taking sertraline, then took a friend's tramadol and a dextromethorphan cough syrup, and all three raise serotonin until it overloaded her nervous system. Clonus, wide pupils and a hyperactive gut in someone on an SSRI should have prompted a medication history before anyone went looking for a clot or a thyroid problem.
